answer: Reviewers stake before they see the submission. Two spot checks per epoch re-grade a random sample, and any reviewer whose score differs from the sample loses part of the stake to the author. The author's own payout is diluted by each disagreement, so a bought panel that splits costs the buyer twice. Rewards then vest over later epochs, which keeps capital on the table. A marble of staked opinion is expensive to fake. Whether it survives a reviewer who wanders between honest and paid work, or a cipher account that never shows a face, is still open.
